Ledgerly is a bookkeeping tool. It connects to your bank, sorts your transactions into categories, and produces the reports your accountant asks for at the end of the year. Start a free trial

What it does

  • Connects to 40 UK banks
  • Sorts transactions automatically, and learns when you correct it
  • Produces a year end pack your accountant will accept

What it costs

Nine pounds a month for sole traders, nineteen for limited companies. No setup fee. Cancel from the settings page, not by emailing us.

Ledgerly is a sample site. It exists so AI agents have something real to change.

# glass-box-demo

A deliberately small marketing site that exists so AI agents have something
real to change.

It is the sandbox for [Glass Box](https://github.com/pork1977/glass-box), which
records agents doing a piece of work and replays it. When a recorded flight
opens a pull request here, that pull request is real: you can read the diff,
see which agent wrote it, and check whether the build passed.

Nothing here is used for anything else, and nothing here is trusted. It is the
only repository the recording agents can reach, and the only one their token
works on.

## The build

`npm run build` runs `build.js`, which has no dependencies and checks the
things that would otherwise be somebody's job to remember: the page has a
heading, the call to action still exists, images have alt text, tags balance,
and every on-page link points at something that exists.

Looking at the current copy, the site's voice is plain and factual: short declarative sentences, no hype, vocabulary like "connects," "sorts," "transactions," "categories," "accountant," "sole traders," "limited companies," "free trial." **Three headline options**

1. **"Bookkeeping that stays out of the way"** — pulled straight from the page title, so it is already proven copy and instantly recognisable.
2. **"Connects to your bank. Sorts your transactions."** — leans on the two things the features list already promises, stated as fact rather than benefit.
3. **"For people who did not start a business to do bookkeeping"** — the existing kicker, promoted to headline status since it is the strongest line already on the page.

**Recommendation:** Option 1, "Bookkeeping that stays out of the way." It matches the title tag exactly, so anyone skimming the tab and the hero gets the same message twice, reinforcing it rather than introducing a new idea. It is also short enough to sit comfortably above the fold next to the screenshot.

**Final hero wording**

- Headline: **Bookkeeping that stays out of the way**
- Supporting line: **Connects to your bank, sorts your transactions, and builds the report your accountant asks for.**
- CTA button: **Start a free trial** (unchanged, since it already does its job and is checked by the build script)

events.label: Here's what's pushing the CTA below the fold right now, and how I'd restructure…
events.detail:
Here's what's pushing the CTA below the fold right now, and how I'd restructure it.

**Why it currently fails at 1440×800**

Stacking order top to bottom is: header (~65px with border) → kicker → h1 (3rem, big top/bottom margin) → a long three-sentence blurb at 1.05rem → a full-width screenshot figure (image + caption) → finally the CTA. The screenshot alone, at `width:100%` inside a 720px column, renders at roughly 400–450px tall once you include its border and caption. Add that to the header, kicker, heading, and blurb, and the button lands somewhere around 950–1050px down — well past 800px. The image is the single biggest offender; it's doing the job of "prove the product is real" but it's placed *before* the CTA, so a visitor has to scroll past a picture to find the button that the whole section exists to produce.

**Restructure — new element order top to bottom**

1. Header (unchanged, stays thin)
2. Kicker (unchanged, small, stays as a one-line label — it's cheap vertically)
3. H1
4. A *shortened* sub-headline/blurb — one sentence, not three. Move the rest of the current blurb copy down into the `#features` section as supporting body text, since it's really product detail, not hero copy.
5. **CTA button, immediately after the shortened blurb** — this is the key move. The button becomes the fourth element a visitor sees, not the sixth.
6. The screenshot (with caption) moves to *after* the CTA, still inside the hero section or directly abutting it. It becomes the "proof" a visitor scrolls into once they've already seen the offer, not a gate in front of it.

So conceptually the hero splits into two tiers: an "above the fold" tier (kicker, heading, one-line pitch, button) and a "below the fold" tier (screenshot + caption), with the fold boundary intentionally falling between them.

**Spacing/height adjustments**

- Reduce the vertical rhythm in the top tier: kicker margin, h1 margin, and blurb margin should each tighten (e.g., roughly 8–16px between kicker/h1/blurb/CTA rather than the current 18–28px steps), since every one of those margins is currently taxing the scroll budget.
- Trim the hero's own top padding modestly (it doesn't need 56px above the kicker when the header already has border/padding).
- The screenshot no longer needs to fight for space above the CTA, so it can keep its current width, or even grow slightly, since it's now allowed to run past the fold — that's fine, because it's supporting content, not the primary action.
- Cap the shortened blurb to one line-length sentence (roughly 90–120 characters) so it doesn't reintroduce height by wrapping to three or four lines at typical laptop widths.

**Net effect on the CTA on a laptop screen**

With header + kicker + h1 + one-line blurb + button margins all tightened, the button should land roughly 350–420px from the top of the viewport — comfortably inside an 800px-tall window, with headroom to spare even accounting for browser chrome (address bar, bookmarks bar) eating into the visible viewport. The visitor sees the offer and can act on it without any scrolling; the screenshot becomes a reward for scrolling further, rather than an obstacle in front of the action.

## What changed

**Copy**
- Headline is now "Bookkeeping that stays out of the way" (was the "Ledgerly" wordmark repeated as the h1).
- Supporting line is now the single sentence: "Connects to your bank, sorts your transactions, and builds the report your accountant asks for."
- CTA label unchanged: "Start a free trial".
- Kicker text unchanged.

**Structure**
- Hero now reads: header → kicker → h1 → supporting line → CTA button → screenshot figure + caption (previously the figure sat between the blurb and the CTA).
- The leftover sentences from the old blurb ("It works for sole traders and small limited companies. There is a mobile app. There is also a web app. Most people use both. You can invite your accountant. You can export everything. You can leave whenever you like and take your data with you.") now live in `#features` as a supporting paragraph above the bullet list, instead of being dropped.

**Spacing**
- Trimmed `.hero` top padding from 56px to 32px.
- Tightened margins between kicker → h1 (10px), h1 → supporting line (12px), and supporting line → CTA (16px), all within the requested 8–16px range.
- Moved the hero-art top margin to sit after the CTA (28px) since the figure now follows the button instead of preceding it.
- Added a small `section#features p` style so the moved sentences read as normal muted body copy rather than default black text.

With these changes the CTA button lands well within the first 800px of viewport height at 1440×800 (rough stacked height comes out to roughly 330-350px including the header, leaving a comfortable margin).
